text:
anya: noticing a weird steady memory climb on long-prefix workloads with MQA Llama variants — not typical eviction behavior, looks like small page allocations keep accumulating :thinking:
anya: repro: run longchat with repeated 32k-prefixes, look at /proc/gpu-kv/stats and runtime logs
anya: sample log snippet:
```
[2024-11-05T22:15:01Z] kv_pages_total=12856 kv_pages_free=432 kv_page_allocs=17234 kv_page_evictions=98 kernel=fallback_mqa slot_map_hits=0
[2024-11-05T22:15:17Z] kv_pages_total=12992 kv_pages_free=178 kv_page_allocs=17648 kv_page_evictions=101 kernel=fast_mqa slot_map_hits=0
```
tom: so evictions are happening but free pages go down, allocs keep increasing — fragmentation?
ravi: can you paste the kernel-selection trace? might be bouncing between fallback and fast kernels causing alias mismatch
anya: here's the trace output from the instrumentation (very noisy):
```
KSEL: req=longseq, seq_len=30720 -> choose fast_mqa (est_latency 9.2ms)
KSEL: page_alloc on node 5 -> fallback_mqa (kv slot stripe mismatch)
KSEL: reclaim attempt -> choose fast_mqa again
```
devon: hmm that stripe mismatch wording is new — sounds like a hashing->stripe mapping disagreement when rope scaling stretches virtual slots
anya: exact hypothesis: when rope scale factor crosses a threshold mid-request, some keys map to new stripe indices; rather than moving existing pages we allocate fresh pages and leave small orphaned fragments around
ravi: that would explain low slot_map_hits. Also explains why evictions increment but free pages still shrink: we evict large contiguous pages but leave many small slabs that aren't reusable due to alignment
ops-bot: perf-alert: long-prefix job #4567 crossed KV growth threshold (rss+vram) 2x baseline at 22:15:18Z
tom: can you run a quick profiling run with kv-alloc debug enabled? set env KV_DEBUG_SPLIT=1 and run `./run_longchat --profile-kv`
anya: ran it, attached the CSV (paste below excerpt) — columns: ts, alloc_count, free_count, slab_frag_pct, avg_slab_size
```
22:14:50, 17230, 520, 31, 4096
22:15:10, 17610, 198, 47, 2688
22:15:30, 17990, 160, 59, 1920
```
devon: frag_pct going up fast. average slab size dropping — many small allocations. likely due to allocation path using redirected kernel on a per-page basis instead of per-chunk. When kernel switches mid-allocation we should try to migrate to new kernel's slab format but we currently just allocate new pages
ravi: two mitigation ideas: conservative kernel stickiness for the lifetime of a request (avoid mid-request kernel flip), and a background coalescer that merges adjacent small slabs when free pages cross a threshold
anya: flipping kernel stickiness on in a canary run reduced alloc churn by ~40% in my quick test
anya: result snippet after stickiness=true:
```
kv_page_allocs delta ~ -40%
slab_frag_pct down from 59 -> 24
request latency +0.6ms p95 (acceptable)
```
tom: good tradeoff. but we need to ensure not losing throughput for short requests; maybe make stickiness adaptive: enable for requests > N tokens or routes labelled long-context
devon: also seen model-specific behavior: Mistral variant rarely flips kernel because its kv slot hash is more stable across rope scales; Qwen tends to alias slots differently under GQA params leading to higher fragmentation when mixed with MQA kernel configs
anya: confirming: same workload on Qwen-GQA produced even worse avg_slab_size numbers and lower slot_map_hits
ravi: for longer term: add an allocator pass to coalesce small adjacent slabs and a periodic compact job triggered when frag_pct > 40 and free_count < threshold
anya: opened a short RFC branch: github.com/redwood/inference/kv-fixes/tree/anya/stripe-coalesce (WIP)
ops-bot: deploybot: canary deployed kv-stickiness=true to dedicated-canary-3 at 22:45Z
tom: after canary run, please gather metrics: slab_frag_pct, slot_map_hits, kv_evictions, p95 latency per route. If we get consistent improvement, schedule for staged rollout
ravi: I'll prototype the coalescer this week. quick note: ensure it respects MQA/GQA page formats — coalescing must verify kernel-format signatures before merging
anya: thanks all. next steps: tom will run broader canary + perf sheet, ravi will prototype coalescer, devon will add unit test for rope-scale-induced stripe remap, i'll continue gathering long-prefix traces
devon: cc @ravi :eyes:
anya: tagging possibly affected customers (PSA) before wider rollout :memo:
